articles.title: Hackers Exploit Cisco SD-WAN Flaw to Steal Encryption Keys
articles.executive_summary: Hackers exploited a critical Cisco SD-WAN flaw to plant custom malware, KeyDrift, designed to steal encryption keys. The attacks are considered historical, but the exact timeframe is unknown.
articles.technical_breakdown: The attackers exploited a previously fixed Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN flaw to plant malware inside SD-WAN network control systems. The malware, KeyDrift, copies and stores encryption keys for later use.
actionable_mitigations: Apply the February patch for the Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN flaw
Implement network containment and firewall rules to prevent lateral movement
Monitor for detection and log indicators of the KeyDrift malware
articles.telegram_snippet: Hackers exploited a Cisco SD-WAN flaw to plant malware stealing encryption keys, using a previously fixed vulnerability.

articles.title: Malware Analysis Lab Data Loss Prevention
articles.executive_summary: A malware analysis lab may lose data if a VM is reverted to a previous snapshot, highlighting the need to store data outside the VM. This issue can be mitigated by implementing proper data backup and storage procedures.
articles.technical_breakdown: The issue arises from the fact that changes made to a VM are lost when reverting to a previous snapshot. To prevent data loss, data should be stored on a separate, external system.
actionable_mitigations: Implement data backup and storage procedures to ensure data is stored outside the VM
Use version control systems to track changes and maintain a record of all data
articles.telegram_snippet: Malware analysis lab data loss prevention: store data outside the VM to prevent loss when reverting to previous snapshots.
